slides.texte_overlay:
How to get really good
at being alone
Take yourself out on a date. A good restaurant, a film, a museum. Doing alone what you'd normally do with others builds a quiet, solid confidence.
Build a routine you enjoy. Cooking, training, reading, a long walk. When your days have structure, time alone feels peaceful instead of empty.
Learn to sit with silence. No music, no podcast, no scrolling. Ten minutes of quiet thinking helps you understand what you actually want.
Start a solo project. Build furniture, learn an instrument, write a story. Projects make alone time productive and give you something to be proud of.
Before: being alone meant scrolling for hours. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and my quiet evenings feel rich now.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: being alone meant scrolling for hours. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. My quiet evenings feel rich now.

slides.texte_overlay: Travel alone at least once. A weekend in a new city with nobody to rely on teaches you more about yourself than years of routine.
Know the difference between solitude and isolation. Enjoy time alone, but keep friends close. The best men are good alone and great with others.
